REPORT

Subject Chinese employee of Cathay Foundry, Ltd., assaulted on Pingliang
Road Bridge by J.M.I.P. Sentry.

Made by D.S. Craig. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

At 6.25 p.m. 14/4/39, Mr. J.H. Prinold,
(British), Manager of the Cathay Foundry, Ltd.,
(British), reported at the station that at 6.10 p.m.
even date, a Cathay Foundry M/truck proceeding west
on Pingliang Road, driven by Koh Dien Yue (郭殿宇),
34, Kiangsu, residing 267 Ferry Road was stopped on
Pingliang Road Bridge by J.M.I.P. sentries who
ordered the driver from the m/truck.

The driver obeyed the order and produced
his pass and after examining same the sentry slapped
him on the face, three or four times then returned
his pass and allowed him go.

No visible sign of injury that would require
medical treatment.

On being questioned, Koh Dien Yue, holder of
Driving Permit No. 13701, stated that at 6.10 p.m.
14/4/39 he was driving m/truck, Lic. No. 16430,
transporting the day workers, then off duty, from
the Cathay Laundry to Thorburn Road and when
approaching Pingliang Road Bridge he slackened his
speed and saluted the J.M.I.P. sentry. As the
sentry appeared to take no notice he kept driving
slowly forward and when several yards past, the
sentry called him to stop and turn back which he did.
The sentry then inspected all the coolies' passes after
which Koh Dien Yue's pass was also examined and
returned to him the sentry slapping his face three
times. He has made a statement to that effect,
copy of translation attached.

报告

事由：国泰铸造有限公司（Cathay Foundry, Ltd.）华籍雇员在平凉路桥遭日本海军陆战队哨兵殴打。

由 D.S. Craig 撰写。由 [签名] 转呈

先生，

1939年4月14日下午6时25分，英籍人士、国泰铸造有限公司（英资）经理 J.H. Prinold 先生来本巡捕房报案称，当日下午6时10分许，一辆由郭殿宇（Koh Dien Yue，34岁，江苏人，住斐伦路267号）驾驶的国泰铸造有限公司机动卡车沿平凉路向西行驶，在平凉路桥被日本海军陆战队（J.M.I.P.）哨兵拦停，哨兵命令司机下车。

司机服从命令，出示通行证，哨兵查验后扇了其耳光三四下，随后归还通行证并放行。

未见需要医疗救治的明显伤痕。

经讯问，持有驾驶执照第13701号的郭殿宇陈述称，1939年4月14日下午6时10分，他驾驶牌照号为16430的机动卡车，将国泰洗衣房（Cathay Laundry）下班的一批日班工人运送至韬朋路（Thorburn Road）。当驶近平凉路桥时，他减速并向日本海军陆战队哨兵敬礼。因哨兵似乎未予理会，他便继续缓慢前行，驶过数码后，哨兵喝令他停车并返回，他照办了。哨兵随后检查了所有苦力的通行证，接着也查验了郭殿宇的通行证并予以归还，期间哨兵扇了他三次耳光。他已就此作出供词，附译文副本。

(批：C 1/4)

Enquiries revealed that the assault was
witnessed by To Kyung Sung ( 朱 金 生 ), coolie,
employed at the Cathay Laundry, residing at No. 6
Loong Yi Li, Pingliang Road and several other Cathay
Laundry employees.
Enquiries by J.D.S. 83 Conno at Pingliang
Road Bridge ascertained from J.N.I.P. sentry named
Kato, 1st Class Seaman, that a m/truck carrying a
number of Chinese, unaccompanied by a Foreigner or
Japanese, was being driven over the bridge without
stopping to show their passes when he called upon
the driver to stop. The driver(Chinese) obeyed the
order and stopped approximately 30 yards west of the
bridge. The aforementioned sentry went forward to
the m/truck took the driver's pass then made all the
Chinese alight from the m/truck and examined their
passes following which he stated that he had slapped
the driver on the face three times with his open hand,
at the same times warning him that in future he must
always stop to enable sentries to examine his pass
and the passes of any other Chinese who may be on
the vehicle. Following this warning the sentry
returned the pass to the driver and allowed him to
drive his m/truck away.

My name is Koh Dien Yue (郭殿宇), age 35, native
of Tsingkong, employed as a driver, Driving Permit No.
13701, by the Cathay Laundry, Ltd., 1178 Pingliang Road,
and residing at No. 267 Tsha Ka Zah, Penang Road.

At 6.10 p.m. 14/4/39, I drove m/truck, Lic. No.
16430 from the Cathay Laundry transporting the day workers
to Thorburn Road and when approaching the Ping liang Road
Bridge I slackened speed and simultaneously saluted the
Japanese sentry on duty at t he bridge. As the Japanese
sentries did not appear to take any notice I kept driving
slowly forward and after passing the sentry he shouted me
to stop and come back, which I did. The Japanese sentry
then ordered every one on the truck to alight. After the
Japanese sentry had inspected all the coolies' passes he
slapped me on the face three times. I do not know the
reason why my face was slapped.

This is my true statement.

Signed, crossmarked and
finger-printed by Koh Dien Yue.

Subject Assault on employees of the Cathay Laundry Ltd., (British) No. 1178
Pingliang Road by Japanese Sentries at Pingliang Road Bridge.

Made by D. S. I. Smith Forwarded by B. Thomas, Supt.

Sir,

At 8.30 a.m. 22/3/39 Mr. J. H. Prinold, British,
manager of the Cathay Laundry No. 1178 Pingliang Road,
came to this station and reported that on the night of
the 21/3/39 and the morning of the 22/3/39 two of his
male Chinese employees were assaulted by the Japanese
Naval Landing Party Sentries posted at Pingliang Road
Bridge.

Enquiries made by C. D. S. 103 and the undersigned
ascertained the following.

At 5.15 p.m. 21/3/39 a chauffeur in the employ of the
Cathay Laundry Ltd., named Wong Kwen (王坤), age 39
years, native of Shantung, driving permit No. 2673 was
driving the laundry M/Truck, S. M. C. Lic. No. 15761 in a
westerly direction over Pingliang Road Bridge carrying
laundry workers home when he stopped, as was his usual
custom to recognise the Japanese sentries posted at the
bridge. The sentry ignored him and when he was about to
proceed on his way the sentry called him to halt and
ordered every one to alight from the M/Truck. (About 40
male and female workers in all).

Immediately after alighting from the truck the
chauffeur approached the sentry and at the same time
bowd to him. The sentry is alleged to have pushed the
chauffeur in the sentry box at the foot of the bridge
where he struck him on the forehead with his knuckles.
The sentry is further alleged to have ordered the
chauffeur to kneel in the sentry box for about 15 minutes
after which he was allowed to proceed.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH）
（批：DesB FILE）
（批：P. A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.) 21/3）

事由：英国企业国泰洗衣有限公司（地址：平凉路1178号）雇员在平凉路桥遭日本哨兵殴打。

由 D. S. I. Smith 撰写，由警司 B. Thomas 转呈。

先生，

1939年3月22日上午8时30分，英籍人士、平凉路1178号国泰洗衣房经理 J. H. Prinold 先生来到本巡捕房报案称，1939年3月21日晚及3月22日上午，他的两名华籍男雇员遭到驻守平凉路桥的日本海军陆战队哨兵殴打。

经刑事侦探警佐 103 号及具名人调查，查明情况如下。

1939年3月21日下午5时15分，受雇于国泰洗衣有限公司的司机王坤（Wong Kwen），39岁，山东人，驾驶执照号2673，驾驶牌照号为 S. M. C. 15761 的洗衣房机动卡车，沿平凉路桥向西行驶，运送洗衣工人回家。途中他像往常一样停车，向驻守桥头的日本哨兵致意。哨兵未予理睬，当他准备继续前行时，哨兵喝令他停下，并命令所有人从机动卡车上下来。（总共约40名男女工人）。

刚从卡车下来后，司机走近哨兵并同时向其鞠躬。据称，哨兵将司机推入桥脚的哨亭内，并用指关节击打其前额。据称，哨兵还命令司机在哨亭内跪约15分钟，之后才允许其离开。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处）
（批：DesB 档案）
（批：特别处副处长助理 3月21日）

At about 6.40 a.m. 22/3/39 a delivery coolie employed
by the Cathay Laundry Ltd. named Kwer Tuh Zien ( 闞 杜 全 ),
age 34 years, native of Soochow, was passing over Ping-
liang Road Bridge on his way to work when he was stopped
by the sentry on duty there and deprived of his pass.
The sentry is alleged to have asked the coolie in Shanghai
dialect "Is your employer British" to which the coolie
states he replied in the affirmative. The sentry is then
alleged to have further asked the coolie "Are the British
good" The coolie states that to this question he also
replied in the affirmative, whereupon the sentry is
alleged to have struck him twice on the left shoulder
with his clenched fist. The coolie states that he was
detained by the sentry for about 3 minutes.

J.D.9.83 interviewed Sub. Lieutenant Takami Officer
in charge of the sentries posted at Pingliang Road
Bridge and drew his attention to the frequent incidents
occurring at the bridge. Sub Lieutenant Takami stated
he would make inquiries and caution the sentries
responsible and added that he would take measures to
prevent any re-occurrence in the future.

1939年3月22日上午6时40分左右，受雇于国泰洗衣有限公司的送货苦力闞杜全（Kwer Tuh Zien），34岁，苏州人，在上班途中经过平凉路桥时被执勤哨兵拦下并没收通行证。据称，哨兵用上海话问苦力：“你的老板是英国人吗？”苦力称他给予了肯定回答。据称，哨兵接着又问苦力：“英国人好吗？”苦力称他对这个问题也给予了肯定回答，随即哨兵据称用紧握的拳头击打其左肩两次。苦力称他被哨兵扣留了约3分钟。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Wong Kwen (王坤)
native of Shantung taken by me C.D.S.103
at Y'poo Stn. on the 22/3/39 and interpreted by Clerk Chin Cheng Ju.

My name is Wong Kwen, age 39, native of Shantung, M/chauffeur, residing 354 Weinan Road. I am employed as a chauffeur, Driving Permit No.2673, by the Cathay Laundry, 1178 Pingliang Road.

At 5.15 p.m. 21/3/39 I was driving M/truck, S.M.C. Lic. No. 15761, conveying about 40 male and female workers, proceeding from east to west along Pingliang Road and on reaching Pingliang Road Bridge I stopped the M/truck and took off my hat to the Japanese sentry there. As the sentry said nothing I started the M/truck and when I was about to move off the sentry suddenly began to shout. I immediately stopped the M/truck and the Japanese sentry approached the truck and ordered all the male and female workers to alight. I also alighted and approached the Japanese sentry to bow at him, but he pushed me into his sentry box where he struck me on my forehead with his knuckles. The sentry then ordered me to kneel there for about 15 minutes after which I was allowed to drive the m/truck away. The incident was witnessed by all the workers who were in the m/truck.

The above is my true statement.

Signed by cross mark.

王坤

                         翻译
                         XXXXXX    职员 Chin Cheng Ju.

我叫关杜全，34岁，苏州人，机动苦力，住平凉路509弄14号。我受雇于平凉路1178号国泰洗衣房担任送货苦力。1939年3月22日上午6时25分，我离家前往上述洗衣房上班。当我走在平凉路桥上时，看见一名日本哨兵站在桥北侧，我立即向他鞠躬并出示通行证。此时日本哨兵从我手中拿走通行证，并用上海话问我：“你的老板是英国人吗？”我给予了肯定回答。日本哨兵接着问我：“英国人好吗？”我也给予了肯定回答。之后他用右拳紧握击打我的左肩两次。我被哨兵扣留了约三分钟，随后便前往工厂。
以上是我的真实供词。

Sir,

Japanese Naval Authorities and Ewo Mills.

of Aug 7
On the forenoon Mr. Pollock (Jardine's), D.O. "D"
and I had an interview with Capt. Maruo, in immediate
command of Eastern District, in the matter of verbal
intimation given by the Landing Party Hannen Road Office to
Ewo Mill Manager that sentries would no longer recognize
Ewo passes as hitherto and that application for new passes
should be made immediately. The intimation was accompanied
by the usual threats of arrest of mill operatives who would
not be permitted to again work for Ewo and would more or
less disappear.

Captain Maruo, whom I usually find more reasonable
than many of his colleagues, expressed the opinion that there
must have been some misunderstanding as he saw no reason for
new passes and was satisfied with those at present carried
by Ewo workers. To ensure there would be no hitch about
the matter, it was suggested to Capt. Maruo that a police
officer should escort the workers to the mill in the morning
and back to their quarters in the evening. I mentioned that
this suggestion was put forward as a sort of guarantee that
the persons escorted were in fact Ewo workers. The Captain
readily agreed to this. He also acceded to my request that
if at any time he had any information or contemplated any
action detrimental to Ewo he would give good notice to D.O."D".

The result of these deliberations appeared satisfactory
to Mr. Pollock.

It is rather curious that Hannen Road should have
picked on Ewo and Ewo alone, as no other industrial concern
has had similar intimation or threats.

关于8月7日
上午，怡和洋行的Pollock先生、“D”区警官和我本人就汉密尔顿路（Hannen Road）办事处向怡和纱厂经理发出的口头通知一事，采访了东区指挥官Maruo上校。该通知称，哨兵将不再像以往那样认可怡和纱厂的通行证，并要求立即申请新通行证。该通知伴随着惯常的威胁，即如果不被允许再次为怡和纱厂工作，工厂操作工将被逮捕，并且可能会“消失”。

Maruo上校通常比他的许多同僚更为通情达理，他认为这中间一定存在某种误会，因为他看不出需要新通行证的理由，并对怡和工人目前持有的通行证感到满意。为确保此事顺利进行，有人向Maruo上校建议，由一名警官在早晨护送工人进厂，并在晚上护送他们回宿舍。我提到，提出这一建议是为了作为一种保证，确保护送的人员确实是怡和工人。上校欣然同意了这一点。他还答应了我的请求，即如果他有任何情报或计划采取对怡和不利的行动，他会提前充分通知“D”区警官。

这些商议的结果似乎令Pollock先生满意。

奇怪的是，汉密尔顿路办事处单单挑中了怡和纱厂，因为其他工业企业均未收到类似的通知或威胁。

Sir,

At 1 p.m. 4.8.38 a telephone message was received from
Mr. McAllen reporting that Japanese Marines had arrested a
number of coolies on the Shanghai Hongkew Wharf.

On receipt of the above telephone message Insp. Palmer,
D.S.I. McCahey, S.I. Nakano and the undersigned immediately
proceeded to the Shanghai Hongkew Wharf and therein interviewed
the informant with the result that the following was ascertained:

At about 11.30 a.m. 4.8.38 whilst a number of coolies were
crossing Chaoufoong Road from the rear gate of the lower
Shanghai Hongkew Wharf to the side entrance of the upper
Shanghai Hongkew Wharf, a distance of about 15 yards they were
halted by a Japanese marine sentry who demanded to see their
passes. The coolies in question endeavoured to explain to the
sentry that they were employed by the Shanghai Hongkew Wharf
and that they did not possess any individual passes.

Whether or not this was understood by the sentry cannot
be ascertained but at this juncture he became very excited
and waived his arm and rifle in a threatening manner thus the
coolies became frightened and all but four ran into the upper
Shanghai Hongkew Wharf.

After the lapse of a few seconds the sentry in question
also entered the Shanghai Hongkew wharf and therein prevented
the coolies from carrying out their respective labours and
apprehended 19 male Chinese namely:

It may be pointed out that the instructions carried out
in the Eastern Area were not directed at British Concerns as
the employees of the Fung Dah No. 2 Mill were also stopped and
if no pass was produced they were likewise arrested.
Five P.W.D. ordure coolies were also amongst the arrests
but on Police representations they were allowed to go but the
Foreigner in Charge of the Section was informed that proper
passes were required.
Fifteen temporary members of the Aquarium staff were also
arrested these workers only being temporary hands taken on,
on 20/7/38 no passes have been obtained. Through negotiations
7 coolies were returned whilst the others were sent South of
the Creek by the J.M.L. Party after their enquiries were completed.
It is apparent to the Police that the precautions taken
by the J.M.L. Party are in connection with recent information
obtained by them that undesirable characters are filtering into
the Northern & Eastern Areas. Many people residing in this area
at present are without residential or visiting passes.
D.C. Special Branch informed of the incident & action
taken.

Subject Interference of Chinese employees of foreign firms by Japanese
Military in Pootung.

Made by D.S. Stevens Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
Investigation into the above was continued at 3 p.m.
3/6/38 when the undersigned visited the Shanghai Power Co., the
Borden Egg Co., and the China Soap Works, in the Y'poo
district. At each of these concerns, the foreign representa-
tive of the company, interviewed, stated that the position had
definitely improved, they having received no reports from
their workers regarding molestation, assault etc, of the
employees whilst in Pootung, nor did these employees experience
their former difficulty in passing the Japanese sentries posted
at the Pootung jetties.

Mr. Davies, however, when interviewed at the Ewo Cotton
Mill, Wetmore Road, pronounced the situation to be worse than
before. Owing to the uncertainty regarding the attendance of
his employees resident in Pootung, he had been forced, he stated,
during the past few weeks to dispense with some two hundred
female workers and to endeavour to recruit the labour from
Shanghai. This had led, he continued, to the partial closing
down of one of the most vital departments in the factory, the
"Winding department", with a consequent loss of output.

According to reports received by Mr. Davies, "Ta Toa" Police
and Japanese Military, in Pootung, had persistently attempted to
influence his employees against working for a British firm and
had continually obstructed them at jetties etc.

I am, Sir,

呈报人：D.S. Stevens 转呈人：[签名]

先生，
对上述事项的调查于1938年6月3日下午3时继续进行，当时本报告人走访了位于杨树浦区的上海电力公司、博登蛋品公司（Borden Egg Co.）和中国肥皂厂。在这些每家机构中，接受问询的公司外籍代表均表示，情况已明确好转，他们未收到任何关于员工在浦东期间遭受骚扰、殴打等的报告，这些员工在通过驻守在浦东码头的日本哨兵时，也未再经历以往的困难。

然而，在威妥玛路（Wetmore Road）的怡和纱厂（Ewo Cotton Mill）接受问询时，Davies 先生宣称局势比以前更糟。他表示，由于居住在浦东的员工出勤情况不确定，他在过去几周内被迫解雇了约两百名女工，并试图从上海招募劳动力。他接着说，这导致工厂最关键的一个部门——“卷线部”（Winding department）部分停工，从而造成产量损失。

根据 Davies 先生收到的报告，驻守浦东的“大托”（Ta Toa，音译）警察和日本军方一直试图煽动他的员工不为英国公司工作，并一直在码头等地阻挠他们。
